title: Progressive private control-plane version curator and upgrade orchestrator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Build an orchestrator that performs progressive version rollouts of the private (VPC) control plane with automated validation gates, Terraform-driven change execution, and well-defined rollback semantics. This ticket focuses on the version curation model, canary cohorts, health-check integration, and the Terraform modules / runbook required to execute upgrades safely across customer VPCs.

Context:
- Private deployments require controlled upgrade paths to avoid disrupting tenant workloads; teams currently run ad-hoc scripts and manual gating.
- We need a reproducible, auditable flow that is compatible with our private control plane operator and with existing Terraform IaC modules.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria:
1) Version curator service that maintains a per-region, per-variant allowed-version matrix (manual overrides via Console + API).
2) Terraform module updates and a new 'upgrade-plan' module that can create an immutable rollout object and produce a planfile for the operator.
3) Canary cohort orchestration: phased cohorts (shadow, 1%, 10%, 50%, full) driven by the planfile and guarded by health gates. Cohort sizes are configurable per-customer.
4) Health gates integrated with telemetry: control-plane heartbeats, reconciliation success rate, API latency P95, and operator errors. Each gate must be pluggable and expressed as a simple boolean condition evaluated against a metrics query.
5) Automated rollback trigger with drift detection and a staged rollback path.
6) Observable runbook: per-upgrade timeline, per-cohort metrics dashboard links, and an audit trail of Terraform plan/apply PRs.
7) Unit and integration tests: Terraform plan validation, operator dry-run in a staging fleet, and chaos test harness for forced component failures.

Design notes / Approach:
- Version curator: lightweight service (Go) backed by a Dynamo table and an internal API. Exposes the active version matrix and accepts curated releases. Console will call curator API for manual promotions.
- Upgrade plan generation: extend terraform-private-modules repo with an 'upgrade-plan' resource that emits a JSON planfile (cohorts, timeouts, health gates, rollback policy). Planfile stored in S3 and referenced by the operator.
- Operator execution: the operator watches planfiles and orchestrates kube-operator actions in each private control plane instance. Operator uses staged feature flags to allow shadow deployments before traffic promotion.
- Health gates: implement a gate runner that queries Prometheus/metrics backend and evaluates configured thresholds. Gate failures halt progression and annotate the plan in S3.
- Rollback: the planfile includes reverse-version pinning and a two-step rollback (soft roll-forward to previous canary, then full rollback if metrics remain degraded).

Security & Compliance:
- All planfiles are signed with a KMS key. Terraform applies for private upgrades must be executed by a service principal with scoped IAM permissions. Audit logs are required for all state transitions.

Testing & Staging Plan:
- Stage 1: unit tests for curator and gate runner.
- Stage 2: end-to-end in a small staging fleet (5 private control planes) using canary sizes tuned to the fleet.
- Stage 3: chaos injection (network partitions, operator crash) to validate rollback and recovery paths.

Deliverables:
- RFC doc linked in ticket comments with sequence diagrams and planfile schema.
- Terraform module PR and example repo usage.
- Curator service + migrations.
- Operator enhancements to consume planfile, enforce gates, and emit events.
- Runbook with dashboard links and run criteria.

Open questions / Trade-offs:
- Where to store planfiles long-term (S3 vs Object store in the control plane DB) — S3 preferred for retention and cross-account access but requires tighter IAM scoping.
- Degree of automation vs manual approval at the 10% -> 50% jump. Default will be gated automation with an opt-in automated promotion flag.
- Backwards compatibility with older operator versions: we will emit a compatibility version in the planfile and require operator >= 2.3 for automated rollouts.
